pr_title: Handle not compatible parameters to IndexOf
pr_body:
Fixes ImmutableArray<T> and SortedSet<T> for the following:
* IList.IndexOf is called with a null "value" parameter
* IList.IndexOf is called with an incorrectly-typed "value" parameter

Fix #84565

issue_context.title: ImmutableArray cast to IList does not conform to other collection's usage
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-collections See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Description When casting an ImmutableArray to an IList, calls to IndexOf do not act as they do in other collections. Other collections return -1 for items that are not found, regardless of their type. ImmutableArray cast to IList then IndexOf is called will throw a NullReferenceException or InvalidCastException depending on the parameter passed in. I originally found this when I noticed a Binding in WPF throwing an exception when bound to an ImmutableArray. WPF was assuming that IndexOf on IList would always return -1 for a non-match. ### Reproduction Steps Assuming the following Enum: `enum States { A, B }` The following code will show the problem: static void Main(string[] args) { List list = new List(new[] { States.A, States.B }); TestList(list); States[] array = new[] { States.A, States.B }; TestList(list); ImmutableArray imm = ImmutableArray.Create(new[] { States.A, States.B }); TestList(imm); } private static void TestList(IList list) { list.IndexOf(States.A); list.IndexOf(null); list.IndexOf(new object()); } TestList on ImmutableArray throws a NullReferenceException when ilist.IndexOf(null) is called. If that line is commented out, it will throw an InvalidCastException when ilist.IndexOf(new object()) is called. ### Expected behavior I would expect IList.IndexOf to return -1 and not throw one of those exceptions regardless of the implementing type. ### Actual behavior A NullReferenceException or an InvalidCastException are thrown, depending on whether null is passed as a parameter, or an invalid type is passed as a parameter. ### Regression? _No response_ ### Known Workarounds _No response_ ### Configuration Version: 7.0 OS: Windows 10 Arch: X64 I doubt it is unique to this OS or machine architecture. ### Other information This may be because at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a7f3df9b14d896cda708e2d22f35165737646769/src/libraries/System.Collections.Immutable/src/System/Collections/Immutable/ImmutableArray_1.cs#L1211 the passed in parameter is directly cast to the type in the collection.
Author: star-thoughts
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Collections`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

Looking at the [other `IList` implementations](https://grep.app/search?q=IndexOf%28%28T%29&filter[repo][0]=dotnet/runtime) in the repo, it seems like the common pattern is to include an [`IsCompatibleObject` check](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/19ff97834663497ff6fd5207f6f64bbe2af93cba/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Collections/ObjectModel/ReadOnlyCollection.cs#L191-L196) in all the methods accepting `object?` arguments.

The only exceptions that I noticed are [`ImmutableArray<T>`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/19ff97834663497ff6fd5207f6f64bbe2af93cba/src/libraries/System.Collections.Immutable/src/System/Collections/Immutable/ImmutableArray_1.cs#L1186-L1212) and [`ImmutableSortedSet<T>`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/19ff97834663497ff6fd5207f6f64bbe2af93cba/src/libraries/System.Collections.Immutable/src/System/Collections/Immutable/ImmutableSortedSet_1.cs#L850-L865). It would make sense to update the implementatins for consistency. Would you be interested in contributing a PR?
I should be able to do this.  Though I'm not familiar with XUnit or how to work with forks on Github.  So there will be a learning curve slowing me down.

If I understand your question correctly, yes. I put them in before making the fix and the test was failing until the fix went in.  They are testing for null and "a" on IList<int> collections.
Ah I see, so presumably one of the `factory` parameters being passed by the test converts the `ImmutableList` to an `ImmutableArray`?
The factory parameter creates either an ImmutableArray or ImmutableList depending on what is being tested.
